exposure: Prenatal ultrasound findings (gestational week of primary diagnosis, exact tumor description, presence of cystic sacrococcygeal formation, signs of cardiac failure due to fetal anemia)
outcome: Prenatal ultrasound correlation with postnatal findings
Occurrence of early and late complications in newborns and children (e.g., postnatal death, infection, ileus, disease recurrence, urinary incontinence)
cohort: Sixteen cases of sacrococcygeal teratoma delivered and treated at the University Hospital Brno between 2005 and 2020.
finding: Detailed prenatal ultrasound examination, particularly the presence of cystic sacrococcygeal formation and the absence of signs of cardiac failure due to fetal anemia, are the most predictive indicators of favorable early and late postnatal outcomes and long-term child development in sacrococcygeal teratoma cases.
followup_time: Up to 2 years after birth (for disease recurrence)
